description:
A prospect used to ask a friend for a designer. Now they ask ChatGPT. BrightLocal's 2026 survey says 45% of consumers used AI to find a business recommendation in the past year, up from 6% the year before. ChatGPT hit 900 million weekly active users in February 2026, and its outbound referral traffic grew 206% year over year. The solo freelancer who used to win on referrals now competes inside a five-name list generated by a model that has never met them. Eight tools track who wins that list. None get a named freelancer into it.

This is a done-for-you AI search publicist for one person. The buyer enters their name and category into a free audit and sees the current ChatGPT answer, the third-party pages feeding it, and the sentence their own site is missing. A $299 Placement Sprint runs 21 days and gets them into three source pages ChatGPT already cites: a directory, a roundup, a curated list. The $149 monthly retainer re-checks answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini, ships one new placement per month, and maintains a structured profile page. Priced $50 above the monitoring tools that only ship a score, priced 10x below the GEO agencies that start at $1,500 a month and only sell to brands.

newLayoutSections.Why Now:
Consumers using AI to pick a service provider jumped from 6% to 45% in one year

The buyer behavior flipped inside a single year. BrightLocal's 2026 Local Consumer Review Survey found 45% of consumers used ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity to find a business recommendation in the past year, up from 6% in 2025. Adobe's 2026 consumer report finds about a quarter of customers now name AI platforms like ChatGPT as their top research tool, ahead of brand websites and online reviews. Among people who use AI for research, 42% say they always or frequently start there. ChatGPT itself scaled from 400 million weekly users in February 2025 to 900 million by February 2026, per OpenAI via Reuters. The shortlist step moved. A prospect who used to Google a designer or ask a peer now asks an assistant first.

Google made the timing official on May 15, 2026. It published its first on-record guide to "Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search," naming AEO and GEO as real practices and telling site owners how to compete inside AI Overviews and AI Mode. The category has a name, a Google-endorsed playbook, and a paying agency tier ($1,500 to $25,000 a month) already selling this work to brands. What is missing at the bottom of the market is anyone doing it for one named person. Google Trends for "answer engine optimization" rose 2.5x in the last 12 months and peaked in May 2026, the same month Google published the guide. The market is forming in public, and the freelancer tier is still empty.

newLayoutSections.The Verdict:
Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

The category is priced and funded: Profound raised $155M, Peec hit EUR 650K ARR in four months, and monitoring tools cluster at $80-$399/mo, so a $149 done-for-you tier priced above monitoring and 10x below agency retainers has a clean slot.
Consumer behavior actually flipped this year: BrightLocal shows AI use for business recommendations went from 6% to 45%, Adobe puts AI as the top research tool for 25% of customers, and ChatGPT referral traffic grew 206% year over year. The buyer behavior the pitch depends on is real.
Fiverr is already running public sessions training freelancers to sell GEO services and hosts a live GEO category with $30 to $3,000 gigs, which means a $99 Fiverr audit gig gives the founder a qualified buyer channel from day one, not from month six.
The wedge is defensible for 12 to 18 months because Peec, Profound, and Rankability will not ship a solo tier without diluting their brand-ARPU pitch, so a founder who owns the freelancer voice on X can build a category brand before incumbents move down.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Freelancers do not yet search for this outcome: five queries like 'get listed on chatgpt' and 'how to appear in chatgpt' return zero US volume on Google Ads, so the founder is creating demand one public audit at a time for the first year.
Attribution is not solvable: the service can show the AI answer moved, but cannot prove a booked client, and senior GEO operators publicly call LLM ranking 'somewhat random,' which invites month-3 churn when no work materializes.
Google's own May 2026 AI search guide warns against seeking 'inauthentic mentions' to influence AI answers, so a placement service that leans on paid directories or thin roundups dies inside one enforcement cycle.
This is founder-led sales for 12 months: audits on X, cold DMs, Fiverr grind. A founder who wants a self-serve product will run out of patience before the retainer flywheel spins.

The Opening (Full Market Analysis).text:
The AI visibility market is real and priced. It splits into three clean tiers, and none of them serve the solo freelancer who gets hired by name.

At the top, Profound raised $155M at a $1B valuation and sells to 10% of the Fortune 500. Self-serve Starter is $99/mo for ChatGPT-only monitoring with 50 prompts. Growth adds three engines and 100 prompts. Enterprise runs custom into the thousands per month. Peec AI is $80/mo Starter (50 prompts, 3 models) up to $205/mo Pro (150 prompts, 2 projects), with Advanced and Enterprise tiers above. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit is $99/mo per domain for 25 prompts. Rankability is $99-$399/mo self-serve for agencies. Ahrefs bundles a free one-shot checker with Brand Radar as the paid upsell. Every one of them ships a visibility score, a competitor set, and a citation list. None of them place a freelancer into the source pages that produce the answer.

Below that, GEO agencies retainer at $1,500 to $25,000 a month. They do content, digital PR, entity building, structured data cleanup, and prompt-set expansion, and they sell to brands, not to individuals. Eric Schwartzman's consultancy is a clean example: named brands, professional services, no individual pricing.

At the bottom, Fiverr's GEO category is live and public. Fixed-price projects average $156 at the base and $291 for on-page work, hourly specialists run $30 to $45. Fiverr is even hosting sessions to train more sellers into the category. But the Fiverr work is aimed at small business websites and local SEO, not at getting a named consultant into ChatGPT's recommendation for a category they compete in.

So the buyer path for a solo freelancer today is: use the free Ahrefs checker, learn they are not in the answer, and then have no next step under $1,500 a month. That is the wedge. A $149/mo service that runs the buyer's prompts, identifies the third-party pages ChatGPT is citing, and does the placement work into sources like them, priced above monitoring because it carries labor, priced far below agencies because it serves one person.

The named incumbent to beat is Peec AI. Peec ships fast, sells to marketing teams, and has 3,000+ brands on the platform. They could add a $49 to $79 solo plan tomorrow and swallow the top of the freelancer funnel. They have not, because their ARPU story is built on team seats and multi-project accounts. That inertia is the 12 to 18 month window.

Enterprise monitoring: Profound ($99 Starter, custom Enterprise, $155M raised, Fortune 500 clients). Peec AI ($80-$205/mo self-serve). Semrush AI Toolkit ($99/mo per domain). Rankability ($99-$399/mo). Ahrefs Brand Radar. All ship scores, none do placement.

GEO agencies: $1,500-$25,000+/mo retainers. Content, digital PR, entity building, done for brands. No individual-freelancer offering at any price point.

Fiverr GEO gigs: $30-$3,000 per project, aimed at small business websites and local SEO, not at a named consultant's own recommendation surface.

The gap: a done-for-you service that runs the buyer prompts for one person, finds the third-party pages feeding the current answer, and gets that person placed into sources like them. Priced for one operator, not a marketing team.

Named incumbents can close this gap, but have not chosen to. Peec, Rankability and Semrush could ship a $149 solo tier tomorrow. They do not, because their sales motion targets brands and agencies. That is the wedge window.

Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

The category is priced and funded: Profound raised $155M, Peec hit EUR 650K ARR in four months, and monitoring tools cluster at $80-$399/mo, so a $149 done-for-you tier priced above monitoring and 10x below agency retainers has a clean slot.

Fiverr is already running public sessions training freelancers to sell GEO services and hosts a live GEO category with $30 to $3,000 gigs, which means a $99 Fiverr audit gig gives the founder a qualified buyer channel from day one, not from month six.
The wedge is defensible for 12 to 18 months because Peec, Profound, and Rankability will not ship a solo tier without diluting their brand-ARPU pitch, so a founder who owns the freelancer voice on X can build a category brand before incumbents move down.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Freelancers do not yet search for this outcome: five queries like 'get listed on chatgpt' and 'how to appear in chatgpt' return zero US volume on Google Ads, so the founder is creating demand one public audit at a time for the first year.
Attribution is not solvable: the service can show the AI answer moved, but cannot prove a booked client, and senior GEO operators publicly call LLM ranking 'somewhat random,' which invites month-3 churn when no work materializes.
Google's own May 2026 AI search guide warns against seeking 'inauthentic mentions' to influence AI answers, so a placement service that leans on paid directories or thin roundups dies inside one enforcement cycle.
This is founder-led sales for 12 months: audits on X, cold DMs, Fiverr grind. A founder who wants a self-serve product will run out of patience before the retainer flywheel spins.
